one_liner: AVX2/AVX-512 vectorized quicksort for primitive arrays; beats a ported .NET GC introsort, not std::sort.
what_it_does: C++ port of Microsoft's C# VxSort: an in-place sort for arrays of built-in integer/float types (i16/u16/i32/u32/f32/i64/u64/f64) on x86 SIMD hardware. You instantiate a template class vxsort<T, vector_machine, Unroll, Shift> for a specific ISA (AVX2 or AVX512) and call .sort(begin, end) on a pointer range; there is no runtime dispatch or generic comparator support like std::sort, you pick the ISA and unroll factor at compile time. It builds as a static library (isa_detection.cpp plus per-ISA sources) linked against Google's cpu_features and fmt, not a single header.
how_it_is_fast: Branchless AVX2/AVX-512 vectorized partitioning (the 'partition machine') replaces std::sort's scalar Hoare partition, falling back to an in-register bitonic sorting network for blocks under 1024 elements instead of insertion sort. A depth-limited heap-sort fallback guards worst-case recursion, and an Unroll template parameter (1-12) controls how many vector lanes are processed per partitioning step, trading code size for fewer loop-carried dependencies.
when_to_use: Sorting large arrays (benchmarked 4,096 to 1,048,576 elements) of raw i16/u16/i32/u32/i64/u64/f32/f64 on x86-64 with AVX2 or AVX-512 available
Throughput-bound batch sorts where you can pick the ISA/unroll variant at compile time and don't need a comparator or non-primitive keys
You want per-element latency down for pointer-sized keys (README: int64 drops from ~53ns/elt scalar introsort to ~11.5ns/elt with unroll x8, unverified against std::sort)
You're OK vendoring a small, currently unmaintained C++ codebase (MIT) and rebuilding it for your target ISA
when_not_to_use: Need a drop-in std::sort replacement with comparators, custom types, or non-x86 targets — no comparator API, and NEON/AArch64 support is stubbed (issue #1, open since 2020) but not implemented

Need std::sort-relative numbers to justify the switch — README only compares against a self-ported CoreCLR-GC scalar introsort, not std::sort, and no std::sort numbers are published despite a BM_fullsort.stdsort.cpp benchmark existing in the repo
Care about active maintenance — the default branch's last commit is 2023-05-10; only an unrelated-history 'nextgen' branch has recent (2026) activity
Small arrays under 4K elements (not benchmarked) or workloads needing a stable sort — this is in-place but not stable, and uses a fixed-size internal scratch buffer sized per template instantiation
Want CI confidence out of the box — an open 'Build fail' issue (#2) shows the bench/test build breaking against a newer clang/CMake/googlebenchmark combination

integration.dependencies: cpu_features (Google, ISA detection), fmt; googlebenchmark and googletest additionally for bench/tests only
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (CMakeLists sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20), CMake 3.24+; clang recommended by the README, GCC also handled in CMakeLists
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 or AVX-512 (ISA chosen per template instantiation at compile time); AArch64/NEON detection is present in demo.cpp but the sort call is unimplemented
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each vxsort<> instance owns a fixed-size internal scratch buffer (_spill), so sharing one instance across threads is not evidently safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same job (sort a pointer range in place) but a different call convention: a template class parameterized by type, ISA, and unroll factor, invoked as sorter.sort(begin, end) rather than a generic std::sort(first, last, comp) with iterator/comparator flexibility

gotchas: ISA is selected at compile time via which header you include (vxsort.avx2.h vs vxsort.avx512.h) and the vxsort_targets_enable_*.h wrapper; using the wrong one for the running CPU is a caller error (the demo does its own cpu_features runtime check before choosing)
Only built-in numeric types appear in the benchmark/test suite (i16/u16/i32/u32/f32/i64/u64/f64); no evidence of support for arbitrary structs, strings, or custom comparators

Internally falls back to heap_sort past a depth limit and to a bitonic-network small-sort under 1024 elements — behavior isn't a single flat algorithm the way std::sort's introsort is, though this is invisible at the call site

Open issue #2 shows the benchmark/test build breaking under newer clang/CMake due to a googlebenchmark C-dialect flag mismatch — unrelated to the sort code but relevant if you try to reproduce the published numbers
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this only if you specifically want an AVX2/AVX-512 partition-plus-bitonic-network vectorized quicksort port of .NET's VxSort for raw numeric arrays and don't need comparator/generic-type support; x86-simd-sort, BlockQuicksort, quadsort, and fluxsort all publish real std::sort or std::stable_sort comparisons and are more actively maintained, so prefer one of them when the baseline claim matters or adoption/maintenance risk is a concern.
verified_claims_summary: The README's reported ~4.5-4.8x speedup (e.g., 1M int64: 53.08ns/elt scalar vs 11.54ns/elt with 8x unroll; measured on an AMD Ryzen 9 3950X @3.8GHz in a June 2020 benchmark) is against gcsort::introsort_orig, a scalar port of the .NET CoreCLR GC's introsort — not std::sort. No compiler version is stated, and no std::sort numbers are published even though the current repo contains a BM_fullsort.stdsort.cpp benchmark file.
status_note: Abandoned on its default branch since 2023-05-10 (later activity moved to an unrelated-history 'nextgen' branch); MIT-licensed and small/self-contained enough to vendor, but only 33 stars and an open build-fail issue against its bench/test harness.
